title: Ramakien (Thai Ramayana)
summary: The Ramakien is the Thai retelling of the Ramayana. The best-known and longest version was completed in 1798 at the court of King Rama I, who led the effort to compile it from earlier versions that had survived only incompletely after Ayutthaya fell. It fills 116 volumes, and murals of the story were added to the Temple of the Emerald Buddha.

uncertainty.note: Academy of American Poets dates the completed version to 1798 in the reign of Rama I; the reign is given as 1782-1809 (Thailand Foundation, Cambridge). The compilation effort ran through that reign.

as_recorded.value: the version completed in 1798 at the court of King Rama I

where.modern_name: Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha), Bangkok, Thailand (proxy pin: the site of the Ramakien murals added under Rama I; the opened pages do not give the place of composition)
where.historical_name: Court of King Rama I, Thailand

importance.justification: The Thai national epic, drawn on across Thai performing and visual arts.
